pairs: Militia est vita hominis super terram,
The life of a man on the earth is a battle,
et sicut dies mercenarii dies ejus.
and his days are like the days of a hired hand.
Just as a servant desires the shade,
et sicut mercenarius præstolatur finem operis sui,
and just as the hired hand looks forward to the end of his work,
sic et ego habui menses vacuos,
so also have I had empty months
and have counted my burdensome nights.
If I lie down to sleep,
And next I will hope for the evening
et replebor doloribus usque ad tenebras.
and will be filled with sorrows even until darkness.
My flesh is clothed with particles of rottenness and filth;
et sordibus pulveris cutis mea aruit et contracta est.
my skin is dried up and tightened.
Dies mei velocius transierunt quam a texente tela succiditur,
My days have passed by more quickly than threads are cut by a weaver,
et consumpti sunt absque ulla spe.
and they have been consumed without any hope.
Memento quia ventus est vita mea,
Remember that my life is wind,
et non revertetur oculus meus ut videat bona.
and my eye will not return to see good things.
Neither will the sight of man gaze upon me;
Just as a cloud is consumed and passes away,
sic qui descenderit ad inferos, non ascendet.
so he who descends to hell will not ascend.
Nec revertetur ultra in domum suam,
He will not return again to his house,
neque cognoscet eum amplius locus ejus.
nor will his own place know him any longer.
et ego non parcam ori meo:
I will not restrain my mouth.
I will speak in the affliction of my spirit.
I will converse from the bitterness of my soul.

speaking with myself on my blanket,”

by no means will I live any longer.
